findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. User-data can be retrieved by principals with instance or metadata access and is commonly exposed through source control, creating a direct credential-compromise risk.

SSH (TCP/22) is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. The associated instance is placed in a public subnet with a default route to an Internet gateway, making remote administrative access reachable from any Internet host.

The separately managed EBS data volume has no encryption configuration. Unless account-level default EBS encryption is enforced outside this configuration, data on this volume is stored unencrypted and its snapshots may inherit that state.
This snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured for encryption. The backup can therefore contain the volume's data without encryption at rest.
The bucket used to archive VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log records may therefore be stored without bucket-enforced encryption at rest.
